```{r}
customers <- read_csv("data/customers.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
category_translation <- read_csv("data/category_translation.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
order_items <- read_csv("data/order_items.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## The dataset

One row is one order at Olist website : one order, its customer, its order status, and its delivery days. The file holds `r nrow(orders)` rows and `r ncol(orders)` columns, covering `r n_distinct(orders$order_id)` orders and `r n_distinct(orders$customer_id)` customers.

```{r}
glimpse(customers)
glimpse(category_translation)
glimpse(order_items)
glimpse(orders)
glimpse(products)
glimpse(sellers)
```
## Data dictionary
Customers Table
| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
customer_id	text	Id per order, links orders to customers
customer_unique_id	text	Permanent id of a real customer
customer_zip_code_prefix	number	First 5 digits of zip code
customer_city	text	Customer’s city
customer_state	text	Two-letter state code

Order_items Table
| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
order_id	text	Id of the order
order_item_id	integer	Item position within the order
product_id	text	Id of the product
seller_id	text	Id of the seller
shipping_limit_date	datetime	Seller’s deadline to ship the item
price	number	Item price in BRL
freight_value	number	Shipping cost in BRL

Category_translation Table
| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
product_category_name	text	Category name in Portuguese
product_category_name_english	text	Category name in English


Orders Table
| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
order_id	text	Id of the order
order_item_id	integer	Item position in the order
product_id	text	Id of the product
seller_id	text	Id of the seller
shipping_limit_date	datetime	Seller’s shipping deadline
price	number	Item price in BRL
freight_value	number	Shipping cost 


Products Table
| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
product_id	text	Id of the product
product_category_name	text	Product category in Portuguese
product_name_lenght	number	Characters in the product name
product_description_lenght	number	Characters in the product description
product_photos_qty	number	Number of published photos
product_weight_g	number	Weight in grams
product_length_cm	number	Length in cm
product_height_cm	number	Height in cm
product_width_cm	number	Width in cm

sellers Table
| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
seller_id	text	Id of the seller
seller_zip_code_prefix	number	First 5 digits of zip code
seller_city	text	Seller’s city
seller_state	text	Two-letter state code

## Master Data Creation
 Joining the 7 datasets to create one master data.

```{r}
library(dplyr)

df_master <- order_items %>%
  left_join(orders,               by = "order_id") %>%
  left_join(customers,            by = "customer_id") %>%
  left_join(products,             by = "product_id") %>%
  left_join(category_translation, by = "product_category_name") %>%
  left_join(sellers,              by = "seller_id")

nrow(order_items)
nrow(df_master)

glimpse(df_master)
```

### Missing values

```{r}
colSums(is.na(df_master))
```
## Renaming the column names
```{r}
df_master <- df_master |>
  rename(product_name_length= product_name_lenght,
         product_description_length= product_description_lenght)
```

## Finding Missing data in Delivery days

```{r}
df_master |> summarise(missing_delivery_days = sum(is.na(delivery_days)))
```
`r sum(is.na(df_master$delivery_days))` rows have no delivery days. They cannot contribute to any customer delivered date, so they are dropped. Rows before: `r nrow(df_master)`.

```{r}
df_master <- df_master |> filter(!is.na(delivery_days))
nrow(df_master)
```

Rows after: `r nrow(df_master)`.


## Removing nulls and imputing numeric values with median

```{r}
df_master <- df_master |>
  mutate(
  # Text columns
    product_category_name = if_else(is.na(product_category_name), "unknown", product_category_name),
    product_category_name_english = if_else(is.na(product_category_name_english),
                                            product_category_name,
                                            product_category_name_english),

  # Numeric columns
    product_name_length        = if_else(is.na(product_name_length), median(product_name_length, na.rm = TRUE), product_name_length),
    product_description_length = if_else(is.na(product_description_length), median(product_description_length, na.rm = TRUE), product_description_length),
    product_photos_qty         = if_else(is.na(product_photos_qty), median(product_photos_qty, na.rm = TRUE), product_photos_qty),
    product_weight_g           = if_else(is.na(product_weight_g), median(product_weight_g, na.rm = TRUE), product_weight_g),
    product_length_cm          = if_else(is.na(product_length_cm), median(product_length_cm, na.rm = TRUE), product_length_cm),
    product_height_cm          = if_else(is.na(product_height_cm), median(product_height_cm, na.rm = TRUE), product_height_cm),
    product_width_cm           = if_else(is.na(product_width_cm), median(product_width_cm, na.rm = TRUE), product_width_cm)
  )

colSums(is.na(df_master))
```

### Exploratory Analysis of specific features like - delivery days(target variable), order_id, order_staus,state


### Average number of delivery days

```{r}
df_master |>
  summarise(avg_delivery_days = mean(delivery_days))
```
On an average, Olist takes around 12 days to deliver its orders across all types.

### Average and max number of delivery days for each day of the week

```{r}
df_master |>
  group_by(purchase_day_of_week) |>
  summarise(avg_delivery_days = mean(delivery_days),
           max_delivery_days = max(delivery_days))
```

The average delivery days are roughly similar for different days of purchase.


### Calculate min. and max of purchase year month(by combining year and month as 1 column)

```{r}
library(lubridate)

df_master <- df_master |>
  mutate(purchase_year_month = make_date(purchase_year, purchase_month, 1))
```

```{r}
df_master |>
  summarise(min_purchase_date = min(purchase_year_month),
            max_purchase_date = max(purchase_year_month))
```

### Total number of orders

```{r}
df_master |>
  summarise(num_orders = n_distinct(order_id))
```
There are 96476 orders placed in 2 years

### Total number of orders placed for each day of the week

```{r}
df_master |>
  group_by(purchase_day_of_week) |>
  summarise(num_orders = n_distinct(order_id))
```

Order placed on weekends are less as compared to orders placed on the week days


### Total number of order status

```{r}
df_master |>
  count(order_status, name = "num_orders")
```
110,189 orders were delivered and only 7 were canceled, so the cancellation rate is negligible.

### Mean, median, min and max number of delivery days for each seller state

```{r}
df_master |>
  group_by(seller_state) |>
  summarise(avg_delivery_days = mean(delivery_days),
           median_delivery_days = median(delivery_days),
           min_delivery_days = min(delivery_days),
           max_delivery_days = max(delivery_days),
           sd_delivery_days = sd(delivery_days),
           num_orders = n_distinct(order_id))
```
  
From the above results we can see that for state Amazonas - the average delivery days are much higher (47 days) as compared to the other states. For rest of the states, average number of delivery days ranges between 11 - 17 days

Also total numbers of order in state Sao Paulo is the highest.
